Package com.noorlandmc.NoorEntities.ai.beta

Class MannequinBrain

java.lang.Object
com.noorlandmc.NoorEntities.ai.beta.MannequinBrain
public class MannequinBrain extends Object
Owns a SensorSelector and a pair of GoalSelectors (normal + target) for a single Mannequin and drives their tick loops.

Also owns a Navigator for custom A* pathfinding. Goals can retrieve it via getNavigator() and call navigator.navigateTo(loc) without needing to manage paths themselves.

Tick order mirrors vanilla:

  1. Sensors — perceive the world, write results to PDC.
  2. Targets — acquire or drop combat/follow targets.
  3. Normal — movement, animation, and reaction goals.

Usage: 


 MannequinBrain brain = new MannequinBrain(mannequin, plugin);

 brain.getSensorSelector().addSensor(mannequin,
         new NearestItemSensor(plugin, 8.0, 3));

 brain.getTargetSelector().addGoal(1, new NearestPlayerTargetGoal(plugin));

 brain.getNormalSelector().addGoal(1, new LookAtPlayerGoal());
 brain.getNormalSelector().addGoal(2, new WanderGoal(mannequin.getLocation()));

 // Navigation — from a goal:
 brain.getNavigator()
      .onArrival(() -> ...)
      .navigateTo(targetLocation);

 brain.start();

Call shutdown() when the mannequin is removed or the plugin disables to cancel all tasks and clean up all state.

    • getNavigator

      public Navigator getNavigator()
      Returns the Navigator owned by this brain. Goals should use this rather than creating their own Navigator, so that navigation state is shared and shutdown is handled centrally. Example from a goal: 
      
 brain.getNavigator()
      .onArrival(() -> setState(IDLE))
      .onFail(()    -> setState(STUCK))
      .navigateTo(targetLocation);

    • navigateTo

      public void navigateTo(org.bukkit.Location target)
      Convenience shorthand: begin navigating to target with no callbacks. Equivalent to getNavigator().navigateTo(target).

    • stopNavigation

      public void stopNavigation()
      Convenience shorthand: stop any active navigation without firing callbacks. Equivalent to getNavigator().stop().

    • start

      public void start()
      Starts the brain's tick loop. Safe to call more than once — subsequent calls are no-ops if the task is already running.

    • stop

      public void stop()
      Cancels the tick task without stopping goals, sensors, or navigation. Prefer shutdown() for a clean teardown.

    • shutdown

      public void shutdown()
      Fully shuts down this brain: stops navigation, unregisters all sensors, stops all running goals, clears both selectors, and cancels the tick task.

      Call from your entity's death handler or the plugin's onDisable.

    • isRunning

      public boolean isRunning()
      Returns true if the tick task is running.
